items.title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered Review Update
items.excerpt: The best this already amazing RPG has ever been.
items.content_text: As the fantasy RPG GOAT, it really doesn’t take a whole lot for me to replay The Witcher 3. I’ve happily done so the numerous other times developer CD Projekt Red has revamped this masterpiece, but The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered seems to be the biggest overhaul to the beloved tale yet. A free update for anyone who owns the original, so many different parts of this already excellent game have been improved – from combat to movement to skill progression (not to mention the modernized graphics). After about 10 hours working my way through White Orchard and beyond, it’s already extremely clear that this is the best The Witcher 3 has ever been. Combat is less floaty and enemies are (slightly) less stupid It’s probably not controversial to say that one of the worst parts of this otherwise amazing adventure was the combat. Even after at least a few updates to it over the years, it still mostly felt floaty, a bit on the sloppy side, and enemies were a huge fan of just standing there and waiting for their turn to get decapitated. The modernizations made to combat in this remaster are its biggest step forward, as a whole bevy of tweaks have been made to address various sticking points. Geralt attacks faster and enemies are quicker to match your pace, which makes the process of chopping through your ninth pack of wolves much less irritating. The camera and lock-on functionality have been the highlight so far, as you can now toggle between large groups of enemies with ease, and without the camera losing its mind. I didn’t even use the lock-on system in the original specifically because it was so unreliable, so being able to do so now has taken some serious getting used to. In general, the camera feels much better – less tightly locked to your back so you can handle groups of enemies more reliably (though those darn Neckers still like to sneak up on ya), and so far I’ve encountered far fewer situations where I felt like I was fighting my view as much as I was the monsters. I’ve also noticed some new enemy behaviors that make swordplay more interesting, specifically how they’ll now retreat instead of letting you trounce them with steel, launch less telegraphed counterattacks, and disappear and reappear behind you (in the case of ghost monsters). All that did a much better job of making me feel like I was fighting intelligent creatures. Of course, compared to some of the stuff we see in action games today, I still do feel like the enemy behavior shows its age, and it was never all that great to begin with. Still, this is enough of an improvement to make combat feel much more engaging than it once did, significantly upgrading one of this adventure’s weakest points. Geralt moves so much faster and Roach is less of a cretin Movement is one of those small details that can grate the heck out of you in a massive RPG like The Witcher 3, slowly filling you with rage over the course of hundreds of hours. In the original, Geralt was often slow and had a lot of trouble getting over things. His rigid animations sometimes made me avoid ladders altogether because I just didn’t have the patience for it. In the remaster, Geralt absolutely flies over fences and navigates vertical obstacles with relative ease, to the point where it actually felt weird to see him be so nimble. I recall losing over an hour of progress in the 1.0 version when Geralt fell off a ledge no taller than a barstool and managed to break every bone in his body. This was reduced already in the next-gen update from 2022, but combined with the other speed and mobility improvements here, it almost feels like a completely different game – to the point where I’ve begun to wonder if it’ll make the map feel smaller than before as I get deeper in. Similarly, Roach is no longer the annoying idiot she once was, now sporting much more intuitive controls that make her less likely to get caught on trees (which she now passes through if she’s just brushing against them while galloping), or end up on top of a barn. Most importantly, you can now loot herbs and whatnot without getting off your horse, which is maybe the single best improvement this remaster offers (dismounting every 10 seconds to pick a flower drove me to the brink of madness in 2015). Skill trees are less restrictive A pet peeve of mine in RPGs is when skill trees prevent you from playing around with different builds until you get deep into the progression. This is something The Witcher 3 suffered from quite a bit in the early hours, as so many of the impactful abilities were locked behind walls you couldn’t remove until late in the journey. The revised trees in the remaster take a page out of Cyberpunk 2077’s book by making perks more readily available earlier on, so you can customize how you’d like Geralt to get his Witchering done. I’m still early in my journey on this run, but I’m already happy to see that I won’t have to wait until I’ve invested a whole 12 points in a branch before I can unlock any good skills – so long as I’ve purchased a skill along the route I’m focusing on, I can now progress down a certain skill path with fewer obstructions. Oh, yeah, this remaster looks pretty great too Maybe this goes without saying for a remaster, but this is a pretty massive graphical upgrade, even over the one The Witcher 3 got for the current generation of consoles just four years ago. The lighting is much more dramatic, environmental textures are way more detailed, shadows and reflections are much more consistent across the board (especially on PC), and Geralt’s hair looks way less like a blurry mess than it once did. Again, this is all stuff that you’d hope would be the bare minimum when remastering a 12-year-old game, but it still warrants a shoutout. There’s even a new photo mode for those of you who want to take glamor shots of Geralt in all his new, high definition glory. The one thing caveat here is that performance is still not perfect, and I still ran into a dropped frame or two on both console and PC. It’s a small price to pay for how much better things look, though, especially with the incredibly short load times I saw. And considering that the original had some framerate issues of its own, it’s not like anything has gotten worse here. The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered’s greatest asset isn’t that it adds anything the original sorely lacked, but rather that it removes some of the biggest roadblocks to fun the 1.0 version was saddled with. Combat is more challenging but also easier to enjoy, movement is quicker and less irritating, and revised skill trees allow for more freedom. Even if it doesn’t manage to fix some of the technical issues (plus I’m sure there are some bugs waiting for me to encounter them that haven’t reared their ugly heads yet), it manages to make this classic RPG more enjoyable in 2026, and that’s worth yet another ride down its well-trodded roads.
items.title_en: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered Review Update

items.title: The Moza R5 Racing Wheel Offers 5.5Nm of Direct Drive Force Feedback for an Affordable Price
items.excerpt: Now on sale at Best Buy.
items.content_text: If you're a big fan of racing games, you've probably already got yourself a wheel. But if you're still rocking entry level gear or a belt-driven wheel because you've been held back by the steep cost of direct drive, then check out this new deal. Best Buy is currently offering the Moza Racing R5 Direct Drive Racing Wheel and Pedal Set for PC exclusively for $349.99 with free shipping after a $30 off instant discount. That might not seem like notable savings, but keep in mind that Moza wheels are already affordable to start with and rarely see discounts throughout the entire year. $30 Off Moza Racing R5 Direct Drive Racing Wheel for PC The R5 is not Moza's least expensive direct drive wheel. That honor goes to the Moza R3 , which retails for $279.99 and is not currently on sale. The primary difference between the two is maximum torque: the R5 offers 5.5Nm of force compared to 3.9Nm from the R3. Both are less expensive than other alternatives: Logitech's G RS50 is $600 (for the wheel only), Fanatec's CSL DD Ready2Race Bundle is $540, Simagic's Green Flag Bundle is $600, and Thrustmaster's T598 is $466. Some do offer advantages like a higher torque ceiling or console compatibility, but if value is king, it's hard to beat Moza. So what makes direct drive the gold standard for racing sims? Direct drive wheels connect directly to the motor, which translates to immediate force feedback with zero latency and no lost power delivery from gear or belt-drive resistance. The higher the torque rating, the wider range of sensitivity. The Moza R5 is a big step up in immersion compared to a gear or belt driven wheel, and 5Nm is considered the baseline for bringing out the best of what direct drive has to offer. The Moza R5 bundle includes the wheel (and wheelbase) and pedals. The 11" wheel features an aluminum alloy rim, microfiber leather grips, Moza's signature RGB sequential flow shift light indicator, and a total of 22 programmable buttons. The wheelbase features aviation-grade aluminum housing, intelligent temperature control, and a 15-bit ultra-high resolution encoder. The anti-slip pedals are constructed of high-strength steel and use Hall Effect sensors. The Moza R5 is exclusively for PC The Moza R5 works for PCs only, which means console gamers will need to look elsewhere. This is an excellent wheel for more competitive racing sims like Assetto Corsa, Automobilista, and Le Mans Ultimate. It will also work well with Forza Horizon 6 , although this game is more arcadey than the rest and was designed from the ground up to be controller-friendly. Assetto Corsa EVO , which is currently available as a Steam Early Access release with a final expected release in 2027, is one of the best use-case scenarios. Sadly but not surprisingly, neither Star Wars Galactic Racer nor Grand Theft Auto 6 are expected to release with wheel support (GTA itself won't see a PC port in quite a while). items.title: A Ton of Legend of Zelda T-Shirts Are Getting Price Cuts for Amazon Prime Members
items.content_text: Amazon is discounting a bunch of officially licensed Legend of Zelda shirts this week. The new sale arrives just a week before Prime Big Deal Days , with more than 40 T-Shirts down to $16.99 for Prime Members. Seeing as I couldn't fit every shirt onto this page, I've gone ahead and curated some of the coolest designs. If you're looking for some of the more obscure options available, though, I recommend you browse the full sale yourself . A 15% discount may not seem like much, but it's likely the best price you'll see on these shirts this year. Amazon regularly discounts it's licensed Nintendo T-Shirts, but we rarely see prices this low. If you've been wanting to spruce up your wardrobe, now's a great time to do so with a Zelda gift for yourself . The biggest draw of this sale is that it encompasses such a wide range of shirts. 2026 marks the 40th anniversary of the franchise, and there have been many Legend of Zelda games since the NES version first came out. Because of that, there are a lot of different directions a shirt can take. There are subtle nods to the original game as well as more modern depictions from Tears of the Kingdom . Whatever type of Zelda fan you are, there's a shirt for you getting discounted here. I myself currently own four different Legend of Zelda shirts that a regularly work into my weekly rotation. With that in mind, my two top picks from this sale are variations of T-shirts I already own. The first is a unique depiction of the Hylian Shield and Master Sword. The image is entirely made up of various weapons, characters, and references to the games. If you want something that looks great up close or from afar, I highly recommend picking this one up. My second recommendations is just a simple shirt depicting the Royal Crest in gold. I've gotten more compliments on this shirt from random dudes at the grocery store than anything else I own. It doesn't overtly say "The Legend of Zelda", it just looks like a cool design. Fans of the games will immediately recognize the Triforce, but anyone else will think nothing of it. More 40th Anniversary Legend of Zelda Merch The Legend of Zelda movie isn't coming out until next year, and a new mainline game has yet to be announced. So with that in mind, most of the biggest Legend of Zelda stuff has been centered around the upcoming Ocarina of Time remake . The game is set to release on November 5 alongside a new Zelda-themed Switch 2 console and Pro controller . LEGO has also been teaming up with Nintendo to release new Zelda-themed sets. The first new set was released earlier this year and depicts 'The Final Battle' in Ocarina of Time . Nintendo announced an additional Link & Epona set, but it won't be releasing until spring 2027.

items.title: Rockstar Suggests Disney World and SeaWorld Probably Won't Be in GTA 6
items.excerpt: Rockstar has suggested that GTA 6 probably won't feature some key Florida attracts, such as Disney World and SeaWorld.
items.content_text: Rockstar has suggested that GTA 6 probably won't feature some key Florida attractions, such as Disney World and SeaWorld. As part of a recent Game Informer cover story on GTA 6 , Rockstar Games seemed to suggest that its fictionalized version of Florida, known as Leonida, won't include every iconic staple of the sunshine state. Game Informer asked Rockstar’s senior vice president of environment art, Paul MacPherson, about some key attractions like Disney World, Seaworld, and Universal Studios, and how they would be integrated into the game. MacPherson suggested that not all of those locations will be featured in GTA 6, as they've had to be selective about what they include for the sake of narrative and game design, but maintained that the endgoal is to replicate the true Florida experience. "We have to constantly evaluate the diversity of landscapes, towns, structures, landmarks, vistas, plant species, rock formations and everything else before we work with design and narrative to distill a list down that best works with and serves the game’s needs," he said. "So, while we may not have those exact locations, everything we have is geared to getting that full Florida experience!” Rockstar didn't rule out any specific locations, but the comment does suggest that you won't find every major attraction in GTA 6. GTA 5 allowed players to explore the Venice Beach Boardwalk, which featured the pier and its various activities. Players could ride a rollercoaster and a ferris wheel, but generally speaking, it wasn't anything to write home about. There's no reason to do it more than once, and as a result, building an entire park around something like that may not be the best use of development resources. The game will, however, feature a zoo for players to explore. Animals are a big part of GTA 6 , as the game will include over 170 different kinds of critters, including rare and legendary breeds which can be studied. There will be unique places to explore in-depth, even if there aren't any theme parks. Rockstar also spent an extensive amount of time in Florida, researching the area by living it directly. The studio confirmed that it even visted strip clubs and night clubs as part of its research.
items.title_en: Rockstar Suggests Disney World and SeaWorld Probably Won't Be in GTA 6

items.title: 24 Jump Street Gets December 2027 Release Date, Original Cast Returning
items.excerpt: 24 Jump Street, the long-awaited next installment in the Jonah Hill and Channing Tatum buddy cop franchise, finally has a release date.
items.content_text: 24 Jump Street , the long-awaited next installment in the Jonah Hill and Channing Tatum buddy cop franchise, finally has a release date. Sony has confirmed that 24 Jump Street will release on December 10, 2027, with Tatum, Hill, and Ice Cube all returning. The film was officially announced earlier this year after years of hopes from fans. Despite its title, it is actually the third film; there was supposed to be a third film in the 2010s which would've linked the Jump Street crew with the Men in Black, but plans for the project fell apart. Given the extended gap between films, some thought the franchise fizzled out. However, Jonah Hill and Meghan Malloy penned a script for a new movie, which will be helmed by Rodney Rothman (Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse). It's unclear who else will star in the project or what it will be about, but given the major gap between these movies, it seems likely that the duo won't be able to integrate back into a high school or college. The first two films already made self-aware jokes about the two looking much older than the people they were supposed to be portraying undercover, so it's possible they could just continue to lean into that. With a release next holiday season, it seems likely that shooting will begin imminently in order to hit its launch date. As a result, we may be able to expect some additional casting news any day. It's another win for those who are seeking raunchy R-rated comedies on the big screen, and hopefully, the film succeeds and can send a message to other studios that there's an appetite for other projects like it. Currently, it'll open around the same time as Avengers: Secret Wars, so it may have steep competition unless Marvel pushes that film back.
items.title_en: 24 Jump Street Gets December 2027 Release Date, Original Cast Returning

items.title: Alan Ritchson Confirmed to Star in Helldivers Movie as Release Date Pushed Back
items.excerpt: Reacher star Alan Ritchson has been confirmed to play one of the titular Helldivers in the game’s film adaptation, which is now set to release in 2028.
items.content_text: Reacher star Alan Ritchson has been confirmed to play one of the titular Helldivers in the hit game’s film adaptation, which is now set to release in 2028. As told by Sony Pictures in a September 30 press release, Helldivers’ release date has been shifted from November 10, 2027 to June 9, 2028. Justin Lin, best known for helming several of the Fast & Furious movies, is still set to direct, with Hutch Parker, PlayStation Productions’ Asad Qizilbash, and Justin Lin’s Perfect Storm Entertainment producing the film. As described by Sony Pictures, Helldivers’ story centers on an “elite unit of soldiers — known as Helldivers — who must battle alien creatures threatening to destroy the fictional planet of Super Earth.” Ritchson will star as “one of the Helldivers,” though it remains to be seen if he is the movie’s main character or not. Ritchson was already rumored to be involved in the Helldivers adaptation; a report from Deadline earlier this month stated the six-foot-three action hero was in talks to star. Now that this has been confirmed, we can't think of anyone better to join the Helldivers' ranks and help spread sweet, sweet Democracy through the galaxy, especially given his standout performance in Prime Video's Reacher . The movie could have looked drastically different, and it almost did; Jason Momoa (Game of Thrones, Supergirl) was initially slated to star in Helldivers, but left the project sometime this summer for unknown reasons. First announced in January 2025 , the Helldivers movie was received with mixed reactions from fans, especially after they learned that director Justin Lin is not a gamer. The Hollywood Reporter described this as a "strength" for Lin, saying he "leaned into it" when pitching his idea for the project. Unsurprisingly, this caused an uproar among players... but the CEO of Arrowhead, the developer of Helldivers 2, assured them that he "trusts" Lin with the IP. "We are not Hollywood people, and we don't know what it takes to make a movie. And therefore we don't, and shouldn't, have final say," he said, urging fans to "let him work his magic." We're hopeful that Lin's Helldivers will be just as fantastic of a love letter to the game as Zach Cregger's Resident Evil was to Capcom's flagship horror series. It's a good time for video game adaptations overall, and more are on the horizon, with Legendary's Street Fighter set to hit theaters on October 16. Image Credit: Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images
items.title_en: Alan Ritchson Confirmed to Star in Helldivers Movie as Release Date Pushed Back

items.title: Crimson Desert Charting the Unknown Expansion Delayed Two Weeks
items.excerpt: Crimson Desert's first expansion was only just announced at the State of Play in September with a very ambitious October 15 release date. Unfortunately it seems that target was a little too ambitious.
items.content_text: Crimson Desert's first expansion was only just announced at the State of Play in September with a very ambitious October 15 release date. Unfortunately, it seems that target was a little too ambitious. Pearl Abyss announced that the Charting the Unknown expansion would be delayed by two weeks, in order to "deliver a more polished and stable gameplay experience." But even with this delay, the new expansion is coming remarkably close to the game's initial release, and hopefully the developer will have even more content planned for the future. The expansion comes just seven months after Crimson Desert intially released back on March 19. And while the reception to the game was mixed, a lot of its initial issues have since been ironed out, turning the game into one of the breakout hits of the year. Hello, Greymanes. We would like to share an update regarding Crimson Desert’s upcoming DLC. pic.twitter.com/mKNmYn10jX — Crimson Desert (@CrimsonDesert_) September 30, 2026 This first expansion will expand the game to a new zone, and will bring sea exploration to the already expansive world. Charting the unknown will also bring more robust base building, with the trailer suggesting you'll be able to actually build new buildings, which will only add another hundred hours to my play time. Crimson Desert's Charting the Unknown expansion will now launch on October 29, and will set you back $24.99. And just like the base game, it'll be available on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and PC.

items.title: GTA 5 Modder Taunts Rockstar With Unofficial Nintendo Switch Port, Gets Cease and Desist from Take-Two
items.excerpt: A modder who was porting GTA 5 to Nintendo Switch taunted Rockstar Games and was immediately hit with a cease and desist.
items.content_text: A modder who was porting GTA 5 to Nintendo Switch taunted Rockstar Games and was immediately hit with a cease and desist. The modder, known as Mojso, was planning to bring GTA 5 and GTA Online to Nintendo Switch for modded versions of the console and got a bit cocky. After Rockstar Games recently posted its guidelines for modding (which forbids unofficial ports), the modder posted : "Try me Rockstar, [I don't give a f**k.]" Three days later, the modder's Discord server was taken down for copyright infringement, but it didn't seem to deter them. After many warned them about how litigous Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two are, the modder suggested they aren't worried about it: "Copyright infringement is anything but enforced in Serbia." Less than a week later, the modder confirmed they had received a cease and desist from Take-Two Interactive and thanked the company for its "mercy." As a result, the port will never see the light of day, as Mojso has stated that they don't want to risk any legal issues. "Paralympics Productions is shutting down on October 3rd. Thank you everyone who supported us through tough times and lenghty development. I am sorry for not fulfilling your expectations and leaving you high and dry. I am thankful for Take-Two's mercy so this is the definitive end," they wrote. When people pointed back to the modder's post about taunting Rockstar, Mojso noted that they didn't actually expect Rockstar to do anything. "They tried me," Mojso said . "[What the] f**k [do] you want me to do? Fight with them in court? I wasn't expecting them to hit back hard." The modder had been working on this port using leaked GTA 5 source code, which has resulted in a bevy of other leaks and issues. Ultimately, it's probably in your best interest to not taunt massive corporations that are known for hunting down people that mess with their IP.
items.title_en: GTA 5 Modder Taunts Rockstar With Unofficial Nintendo Switch Port, Gets Cease and Desist from Take-Two

items.title: New Uncharted Game Featuring Nathan Drake Reportedly in the Works at Naughty Dog
items.excerpt: A new report claims that a brand new Uncharted game featuring Nathan Drake is one of several projects in the works at Naughty Dog.
items.content_text: A new report claims that a brand new Uncharted game featuring Nathan Drake is one of several projects in the works at Naughty Dog. MP1st has reported that the next Uncharted game, which is not a remake of any kind, is in active development at Naughty Dog. The game will feature Nathan Drake in some capacity, but it's unclear if he's the lead, in a supporting role, or even just a cameo. The project is being helmed by Shaun Escayag, who previously led Uncharted: The Lost Legacy, a standalone expansion for Uncharted 4. This has been heavily speculated for years now, with Escayag having recently teased the project himself on his socials . The director was in Trindad earlier this year for "research" and posted a picture of a very old-looking cannon. MP1st noted that the new Uncharted game is set to be Naughty Dog's next game following the release of Intergalactic, which is speculated to launch next year. The studio recently confirmed that it will give a proper look at its upcoming sci-fi game in 2027, as well. Additionally, Naughty Dog confirmed it has multiple Last of Us projects in the works beyond the existing HBO TV series. Series creator Neil Druckmann has avoided revealing what mediums these projects will utilize, so they could be shows, films, books, or games. However, it feels like a safe bet that at least one of them is probably a video game, and fans are hoping it's The Last of Us Part 3. The next Uncharted game is expected to be at least a couple of years away. Uncharted 4 was released a decade ago and put a nice bow on Nathan Drake's adventures. However, given that he remained alive and well, the door has always been left open for another escapade. Now, Drake could be joined by his daughter, Cassie, who takes a clear interest in Nathan's same hobbies.

items.title: Beware Boiúna Review
items.excerpt: Beware Boiúna review: You do intend to have a giant snake in your giant snake movie eventually, right?
items.content_text: Beware Boiúna is in theaters on October 2. Movies about monstrous versions of recognizable animals are a fun subgenre. The likes of Anaconda, Lake Placid, The Meg, and the granddaddy of them all, King Kong, offer a certain innate allure regardless of their differing quality, as they take a creature we might already find menacing and mega-plus-size them. Some lean into camp, some into pure horror, and some into tragedy, but a surprising number of them work on some level. More New Movie Reviews Godzilla Minus Zero Review Digger Review The latest addition to this type of film is Beware Boiúna, which has its moments and a few clever twists on formulaic situations, but never quite fully takes off. On top of that, the film also suffers from just taking too damn long to get to the giant snake we’re there to see. I want to beware Boiúna, so give me Boiúna! The film follows a trio of doctors who come to the Amazon on a humanitarian trip to administer medical assistance and, along with the crew of the boat they’re traveling on, run afoul of the legendary Boiúna — a massive fearsome snake from Brazilian mythology who is described almost like a force of nature, dispatching anyone that she sees as upsetting the balance within her home. Though Beware Boiúna delivers a couple of early death scenes to tease the terrors to come, its set-up is far too prolonged for a film of this sort. Even at 1 hour and 44 minutes, it easily feels 15 minutes too long; Anaconda and Lake Placid knew what they were doing, running 90 minutes or less each. There are ultimately too many scenes establishing the characters and their dynamics, along with an attempt to go for a more serious-minded, grounded feeling than you might expect from a film of this sort. It’s admirable to infuse themes about the exploitation of the Amazon and its indigenous people into a giant snake movie, but it should be done far more efficiently or better blended within the mayhem people are paying to see. The film also includes a storyline that feels like it’s part of the set-up to a totally different movie, involving a notably dark experience that med student Alli (Jessica Rothe) and ship mechanic Lena (Kiana Madeira) have that leads to “colonizer” Brennan (Logan Marshall-Green) and his men angrily tracking them from a different boat. Sure, it offers up more potential victims for Boiúna, but it’s another place where there was an easier, quicker way to get there. When Boiúna finally unleashes, she’s pretty cool and very daunting, and the film makes good use of her unreal size as a weapon in its own right… when we can get a good look at her, that is, which isn’t enough. Director Mike P. Nelson and cinematographer Nick Junkersfeld keep Beware Boiúna often looking visually appealing, and the FX used to bring Boiúna are solid in the glimpses we get. But it quickly begins to feel like the film’s low budget is keeping her from being seen nearly as much as one would hope, including resorting to some distracting shaky-cam at points to try to disguise that fact… and this is not nearly a Jaws-level film in terms of making up for its often offscreen beast. Veteran screenwriter Alan B. McElroy, the writer behind Halloween 4: The Return of Michael Myers — still the best Halloween sequel ever — manages to interject some deviations from the expected formula of this kind of movie. There are solid moments that play with the usual flow of who will die next, whose perspective we’re following, or what character we’re meant to like at any given moment. But at the same time, there’s not enough done in terms of delivering memorable deaths, with too many characters taken out quickly and without discernible details to make their demise stand out. There’s not enough done in terms of delivering memorable deaths, with too many characters taken out quickly and without discernible details to make their demise stand out. And yet there are also well-done scenes involving mosquito eggs left inside a human’s back, a snake smashing into a construction vehicle, or the particular highlight of a character needing to think fast to save themselves using the corpse of a fallen friend. But then that scene is undercut by some unnecessary flashbacks immediately afterward, providing hand-holding we simply don’t need to apparently remind the audience of a relationship we are already fully aware of. Ultimately, there’s just a lot of push-pull here. Anchoring the film are the likable duo of Rothe and Madeira, projecting the feeling of believable resourcefulness that these characters need to have. It’s too bad Beware Boiúna doesn’t allow for Rothe to show off her impressively strong comedy chops like the Happy Death Day movies do, but better served on that front is Will Close. Close nails each of the funny lines given to his comic relief character of Callum, who’s very much out of his element even before the giant snake arrives. Director Nelson — recently hired to direct the eleventh Saw movie — shows some flair, including the moments mentioned above or with a couple of well orchestrated jump scares, such as one that cleverly uses blurriness as a set-up. But these “that was cool” beats that are peppered throughout the film never gain enough momentum for the movie to feel like it’s truly locked in. And they can't make up for not having enough Boiúna!

items.title: Ordering DoorDash Is Too Hard, So an AI Agent Will Soon Be Able to Order Pizza for You
items.excerpt: Ordering food through DoorDash is probably one of the biggest examples of how modern life has grown incredibly convenient, but apparently, there are still some people who think scrolling through an app is too much work. Now, you'll be able to just text DoorDash and have it order food for you without needing to figure out what, exactly, you feel like eating.
items.content_text: Ordering food through DoorDash is probably one of the biggest examples of how modern life has grown incredibly convenient, but apparently, there are still some people who think scrolling through an app is too much work. Now, you'll be able to just text DoorDash and have it order food for you without needing to figure out what, exactly, you feel like eating. DoorDash announced the feature earlier this week, and the idea is that you'll text an AI agent through iMessages – apparently Android support will come sometime in the future – an idea of what you want for dinner. Then, DoorDash's AI agent will browse through all the restaurants in your area and give you suggestions based on your past orders and what you included in your text. One of the examples DoorDash includes is asking its bot for your usual Friday night order, and it'll remember what you usually get, along with any modifications you usually make. This is already pretty easy to do within the app, which usually has your last few orders at the top of the screen anyways. Ironically, texting a robot for your usual order might end up having more button presses than just opening the app and ordering normally. In some ways, this actually feels like a blast from the past. SMS ordering used to be a thing, before the rise of smartphones. Dominoes introduced a way to order pizza by sending them an emoji all the way back in 2015, according to TechTimes . Though, to be fair, that was just one restaurant. If you want to cut scrolling through an app out of your DoorDash routine, you can sign up to test this feature on DoorDash's website , but only if you're on iOS. Android users will just have to order food the new-old-fashioned way for a while longer. It's not clear when this feature will leave beta, but either way, it seems like ordering food will get even easier, regardless of whether or not it actually needed to.

items.title: European Commission Calls Out Riot, Activision, Mojang, and More Over In-Game Currency and Transactions
items.excerpt: The European Commission is taking action against nine video game companies over their digital currency and pricing of in-game items with the goal of protecting players’ rights.
items.content_text: The European Commission is taking action against nine video game companies over their digital currency and pricing of in-game items with the goal of protecting players’ rights. Launched on September 29, 2026, these actions are a follow-up to the Consumer Protection Cooperation Network’s Key Principles on in-game virtual currencies, which are a set of guidelines released in March 2025 that “promote transparency and fairness” for in-game currency and transactions. These Key Principles guidelines were reached after the CPC Network had extensive discussions with game studios and publishers — but despite these talks, it found indications that a “high number of video game companies” hadn’t made any substantive changes to their games as a result of its public guidance, “nor as a result of the extensive talks between the CPC Network and the gaming industry that have taken place over the course of the past years.” The CPC Network name-dropped these companies in a joint statement with the European Commission on September 30, publicly asking that they bring their in-game currency and transaction systems in line with their guidelines. These companies include Activision Blizzard UK, Mojang AB, Riot Games Limited, Supercell Oy, and Ubisoft EMEA SAS. “Some video games directly exhort children to make purchases, despite an explicit prohibition in EU consumer protection law. Consumers across Europe should be able to play and interact with video games without being tricked into spending more money or time on video games than they want,” the CPC Network’s joint statement reads. As outlined by the European Commission, its newest actions focus on seven core principles: providing clear and transparent pricing, not obscuring costs, not forcing unwanted currency purchases, providing clear information before the purchase, respecting the right to withdraw, using fair and understandable terms, and protecting vulnerable consumers. The European Commission says that games must now show the actual, real-world price of in-game items that players are able to buy using virtual currency. Additionally, games must not require players to jump through hoops with currency exchanges or use multiple currencies, which would make the actual cost of these items unclear. On top of that, games must not make players “feel obliged to buy an excessive amount of virtual currencies to progress or enjoy the game,” and they should be allowed to withdraw from any contracts within a two-week period, including for “unused virtual currency.” “Roughly half of Europeans play video games, making gaming a major part of our digital economy and everyday lives,” Michael McGrath, Commissioner for Democracy, Justice, the Rule of Law and Consumer Protection, said in a statement . “With that reach comes responsibility. The industry must ensure that its games do not expose players — especially children — to harmful or unfair practices. The game must be fair, and the rules must be respected. National authorities, with the support of the Commission, will make sure they are enforced.” This is the latest big swing from the EU in the video game space after documents outlining the The EU Kids Act was shared online. This proposed legislation would require age verification for several online services, including certain multiplayer games that are “risky to minors.” Image Credits: Unsplash.com - Matteo, Jonathan Borba

items.title: MTG Corn Maze Secret Lair Superdrop Brings Jim Henson's Labyrinth, KPop Demon Hunters, and Marvel Zombies to Magic
items.excerpt: Wizards of the Coast trots out a new MTG Secret Lair on a monthly basis at this point, and while crossovers aren't anything new, the new 'super drop' brings Jim Henson's Labyrinth and KPop Demon Hunters to the card game for the first time.
items.content_text: Wizards of the Coast trots out a new MTG Secret Lair on a monthly basis at this point, and while crossovers aren't anything new for the franchise, this new 'superdrop' brings Jim Henson's Labyrinth and KPop Demon Hunters to the card game for the first time. Wizards of the Coast has just announced the Corn Maze Superdrop, clearly in time for Halloween, but instead of going with a darker horror twist like it did with the Junji Ito drop, all of these collections are relatively lighthearted. Of course, for most people, the biggest draws will be the KPop Demon Hunters and Labyrinth drops – the latter of which has three collections – along with a Marvel Zombies collection. The three Labyrinth drops are the highlight of the Corn Maze Superdrop, though. The Secret Lair x Jim Henson's Labyrinth Fear Me, Love Me drop is entirely focused on Goblin kindred cards, and is headlined by Muxus, Goblin Grandee, a Goblin Staple, posing as Jareth, Goblin King with a beautiful illustration of David Bowie. Of course, there's also a copy of Claim the Firstborn as The Kidnapping of Toby. For some reason, though, this drop also has a copy of Trinisphere, which doesn't really fit into any conceivable goblin deck, but at least it has some cool art of Bowie holding a bunch of orbs . It wouldn't be a Secret Lair Superdrop without some nigh-unreadable cards, and that's where the Secret Lair x Jim Henson's Labyrinth: Through the Labyrinth comes in. The art on these cards are all gorgeous, though I could totally see some of them being hard to parse from across the table. Still, Wizards decided to print Leveler in this drop, which you can combine with The Beamtown Bullies or Thassa's Oracle to make your pod wish they were dropped in the Labyrinth. There's also a KPop Demon Hunters drop, which has some incredible cards with combo potential. This one comes with a copy of Freed From The Real and Underworld Breach, both of which will be notorious in decks that are built around them. There's a reason Breach has been banned in multiple formats, after all. And Wizards is still trying to work more Marvel content into Magic, this time with a Marvel Zombies drop that's focused on Zombie kindred cards. But, as cool as it would be to have a commander deck helmed by Zombie Thor or Zombie Scarlet witch, none of the cards in this drop are really worth the high price you'd be paying for them, unless you really love Marvel Zombies. Some of the other drops are seriously cool, too. The Manufactured Grounds by See Machine drop brings some incredible art to the original artifact land cycle from Mirrodin. That drop probably doesn't make a lot of sense from a purely financial perspective, but damn, does it look cool. Then there's the Peace, Love and Treefolk drop, which gives Timber Protector its first meaningful reprint besides the Lord of the Rings commander decks. I'm probably going to pick up all of the Labyrinth drops, and if you want to grab one (or all) of them too, the Corn Maze Superdrop will be available starting at 9am PT / 12pm ET on October 12. Wizards of the Coast will even toss in a Labyrinth-flavored copy of Maze of Ith on any order over $199.

items.content_text: Emmy-nominated actor Vincent D’Onofrio has somehow found himself at war with a self-proclaimed ‘gooner’ over Deborah Ann Woll’s appearance in God of War Laufey. The next game in the God of War series is fast approaching, this time following the adventures of Laufey, Kratos’ second wife and Loki’s mother in Norse mythology. Given the current state of social media, it’s almost unsurprising that this fact alone has riled up the online rage machine — but it seems the controversy has grown so loud that other A-List actors are taking notice. More recently, the conversation has shifted from Deborah Ann Woll’s in-game appearance as Laufey to her special armor sets within the upcoming game. As told by a Twitter/X user who goes by the name ‘Geralt of Goonia,' Sony’s Santa Monica Studio “would rather go bankrupt than give you an ounce of female attractiveness,” specifically when it comes to how much skin these armor sets cover. Unexpectedly, Vincent D’Onofrio — who acted alongside Woll in Netflix and Marvel’s Daredevil series — chimed into the conversation to defend his co-star and proclaim his excitement to play the game alongside his son when it releases this coming February. “Not that you asked, but… In no way do I agree with you,” he wrote. “Deborah is beautiful and extremely talented. She is as smart as a whip and a complete nerd. Also incredibly kind. How perfect she is! And a good friend. I am a fan of God of War. I, for one, cannot wait to play the new game with my son.” Not that you asked, but... In no way do i agree with you. Deborah is beautiful and extremely talented. She is as smart as whip and a complete nerd. Also incredibly kind. How perfect she is! And a good friend. I am a fan of God of War. I for one cannot wait to play the new… — Vincent D'Onofrio (@vincentdonofrio) September 30, 2026 Despite getting owned by Kingpin himself, Geralt of Goonia continued his tirade, leading to no end of humorous responses and memes from players defending Laufey and agreeing with D’Onofrio’s excitement about playing the game. Laufey has been at the center of a few discussions between notable folks in the gaming and entertainment space lately; the original creator of God of War, David Jaffe, called the game “stupid” during a recent live stream, and accused its creative director, Ariel Lawrence, of having a “lack of passion” for the title itself. (He later clarified these remarks in a tweet and defended Lawrence from the ensuing harassment campaign that started against her as a result of his comments.) Prior to that, The Last of Us director Bruce Straley used Laufey as an example of AAA games that failed to “excite” him, though he similarly clarified this statement and apologized for bringing "uninvited and unnecessary negative attention” to the title. Woll, for her part, hasn’t let the negativity get her down. Speaking with a fan at Florida Supercon in July, she said she’s confident that Laufey is a fantastic game, which has, at least in part, helped her avoid being affected by the backlash from trolls online. "Genuinely, I thought I was going to be much more offended by it, but one, I'm not on social media, so that helps, and two, I don't know, I feel totally unbothered," Woll said. "Because I just know it's great. It's okay if it's not your cup of tea, but in no universe is it bad,” she said. God of War Laufey releases on 16, 2027 exclusively on PlayStation 5. items.title: 'Xbox Is Not for Sale' — Asha Sharma Denies Reports That Microsoft Is Considering Selling Its Gaming Business
items.excerpt: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has denied reports suggesting Microsoft was considering selling its gaming business.
items.content_text: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has denied reports suggesting Microsoft was considering selling its gaming business. In an interview with the New York Times , Sharma declared: “Xbox is not for sale.” “We will do whatever it takes to set the company up for success, and we will look at the right partnerships, the right operating model and everything needed to achieve that,” Sharma continued. One of the big questions emerging from Sharma’s appointment as Xbox CEO earlier this year, and the subsequent layoffs and restructuring that have occurred in recent months, revolves around the long-term future of Microsoft’s gaming business. Will Microsoft sell off Xbox? Are the cuts and restructure laying the groundwork for a sale? Details on a potential shakeup came from The Information (via Reuters ), which said that Microsoft hadn't ruled out turning the Xbox brand into a wholly-owned subsidiary. It said the move could result in Xbox being operated as a joint venture with other partners or even potentially sold. Sharma’s Xbox reset has since become clearer. Nearly 2,000 Xbox staff have already been cut, with more to come this financial year. Multiple studios have either exited Xbox or face closure , and various games have been canceled . Xbox is now focused on fewer, bigger video game franchises such as The Elder Scrolls, Fallout, and Minecraft, with the likes of Halo moved over to Call of Duty company Activision . Through it all, there are question marks hanging over the viability of Xbox’s confirmed next-gen console, Project Helix. While some believe this reset and the cuts that have come with it are part of a strategy to make Xbox easier to sell, analysts aren’t convinced. Some have said Xbox would likely have few suitors interested in buying the business outright, considering Microsoft bought Activision Blizzard for an eye-watering $69 billion, Xbox’s huge payroll, extensive studio setup, and hardware business. More likely, analysts have suggested, is that big companies may pick off parts of Xbox as Microsoft continues to look to trim the business. The NYT speculates that an eventual spinoff could create an independent Xbox that would partner with Microsoft while keeping its costs off the company’s balance sheet. But Sharma cast doubt on this as an option, too, saying: “We’ve got a long way to go with Microsoft, and we’re going to take the long-term view.” Who would even buy Xbox when Xbox itself admits its business is unhealthy? Xbox ended the financial year with a 3% accountability margin (assumed to be profit margin), down year-over-year. Excluding Activision Blizzard King, over the past five years Microsoft spent over $20 billion on ongoing investments in what Sharma called its content, platform, and hardware “subsidy,” but annual revenue declined nearly half a billion during that time. “We are operating at margins that are 3-10x lower than comparable platform and publishing businesses,” Sharma said in a blog post announcing the layoffs in July. “We entered Gen 9 with a smaller install base and a higher cost structure. To grow, we bet on Game Pass, multi-platform, and a broader portfolio of content. While those businesses have created meaningful value, they did not grow at the pace we expected. As that happened, our core business weakened, and we added more teams, more investment, and more time, hoping for a better outcome. And now the industry is facing the most severe hardware crisis in its history. We must reset Xbox.” Meanwhile, Microsoft has increased the price of Xbox consoles. Microsoft blamed this on console storage and memory prices, which have increased by more than 2.5x, and it expects another doubling by the fall of 2027. "The entire consumer electronics industry is struggling with the current components crisis, but the effects are particularly hard on consoles," Microsoft said when it announced the price rises. "... the industry is facing the most severe hardware crisis in its history," Sharma added in the Xbox "Reset" memo. For now, Sharma’s focus is on growing Xbox, which, she told the NYT, still has 500 million players a month. Microsoft's ambitious target is for Xbox to reach 1 billion people a day — a figure that has been ridiculed online. How will Xbox achieve this? By tapping into markets such as Africa and South Asia via cloud computing, and investing in Minecraft as a Roblox competitor, the NYT reported.
